excerpt: See how Dubai apartment service charges affect net rental returns and learn which unit-specific documents and approved rates to check.
introduction:
Service charges can materially change the net income from a Dubai rental apartment. Two units with similar rent and purchase costs may leave different amounts for the owner when their building charges differ. Compare the approved charge and the services it funds for the exact unit, rather than relying on a neighbourhood average.

The worked comparison below uses sample figures. It illustrates the effect of a charge, not the actual cost or return of any Dubai building.
takeaways: Check the approved charge, area basis, statement and arrears for the specific apartment.
Deduct owner-paid service charges from rent after a vacancy allowance when calculating operating income.
A lower charge is not automatically better if it buys different services or a building has unresolved maintenance needs.

sections.heading: What does the service charge cover?
sections.body:
A service charge funds approved costs associated with common areas and facilities. Depending on the property and budget, these can include shared cleaning, security, lifts, maintenance and management. Ask for the approved budget and the exact scope rather than assuming every building covers the same items.

DLD's [service charge index](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/service-charge-index/) provides a way to check approved charges. Its [FAQs](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/frequently-asked-questions) explain that charges differ between projects and discuss using the approved rate and unit area to estimate the amount. Confirm the relevant area basis, period and current unit statement with management and DLD.

A building service charge is distinct from electricity or cooling billed to the apartment and from a manager's fee for handling a tenancy. Check what the lease assigns to each party.

sections.heading: See the effect on net income
sections.body:
Assume two sample apartments each cost AED 1,050,000 including acquisition costs, have AED 90,000 annual rent, AED 7,500 vacancy allowance and AED 9,000 in other owner operating costs. Unit A has an assumed AED 6,000 service charge; unit B has AED 18,000.

Unit A's net operating income is AED 67,500, or approximately 6.43% of the total acquisition cost. Unit B's is AED 55,500, or approximately 5.29%. The AED 12,000 difference in annual income comes solely from the assumed charge difference. The worked examples show how different service charges affect the income remaining for an owner.

The chart compares the resulting income. It excludes mortgage payments, tax, changes in property value and selling costs; those need separate analysis.

sections.heading: Why might two buildings differ?
sections.body:
The range and cost of facilities, size of common areas, maintenance requirements and approved budget can vary. A pool, gym, extensive landscaping or specialist equipment may require ongoing upkeep. Ask what the charge funds and inspect the actual shared facilities.

A low current charge is not proof that a building is inexpensive to maintain indefinitely. Review the management statement, condition, repair history and any available information on reserves or planned work. Likewise, a higher charge should be assessed against the services and condition actually provided.

Compare the same annual period and the same area basis. If a figure is quoted per square foot, check the approved unit area and whether any other approved charge is separate. Calculate charges using the approved rate and the registered area for the apartment in question.

sections.heading: Include it in a complete yield calculation
sections.body:
Start with expected rent based on comparable signed leases, subtract a vacancy allowance and all owner-paid operating costs, then divide by the full acquisition cost. The [Dubai net rental yield guide](/journal/how-to-calculate-net-rental-yield-in-dubai) explains the arithmetic and distinguishes it from gross yield and mortgage cash flow.

If a lease requires a tenant to pay a particular utility or service, confirm the written terms and avoid deducting the same cost twice. Ask whether management and other provider quotes include applicable tax. Keep a separate reserve for repairs inside the apartment that common-area charges do not cover.

Stress-test a higher future charge and a longer vacancy. A current approved amount is an input for the stated period, not a promise that it will never change.

sections.heading: Check the position before transfer
sections.body:
Request a current statement for the unit, evidence of payment and any arrears or clearance required for the sale. Agree in writing how charges for the period around transfer will be settled. DLD's [property sale registration service](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/property-sale-registration/) lists an e-NOC for applicable freehold-area transfers; confirm the current procedure and any property-specific conditions.

If the apartment is tenanted, inspect the lease and understand what the buyer will assume. Ask management whom to contact for statements and defects after transfer. Verify the buyer's ownership right and other transaction costs separately.

The [JVC and Arjan area guide](/journal/jvc-vs-arjan-apartment-investment-comparison) shows how building-level checks fit into a wider area comparison.

sections.heading: Review the charge after purchase
sections.body:
Keep each annual statement and compare it with the approved budget and services delivered. Record due dates, receipts and the management contact, and ask for clarification if the area basis or charge changes. A dated record helps you update your rental budget and understand any amount outstanding when you later sell.

Inspect shared areas periodically and report a maintenance issue through the building's documented process. Service charges and the condition of facilities can both matter to a tenant's experience and to a future buyer, but they do not by themselves establish the rent or resale value of an apartment.

sections.heading: Compare current apartments
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Dubai project collection](/projects?emirate=Dubai) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget and intended use. Ask which specific units are available and request their current service-charge statements, price and terms.

Use verified unit-level figures in your own calculation and obtain current official confirmation where needed. The examples above do not establish the cost or yield of a real building.
